## Architecture
{2-3 sentences describing the architectural style: hexagonal, layered, modular monolith, microservices, etc.}

**Example:**
> Hexagonal architecture. Domain layer has zero Spring annotations. Use cases in `application/`
> call Port interfaces — never concrete adapters. Controllers and Kafka consumers are adapters in
> `infrastructure/`.

### Package Structure
```
com.{company}.{project}/
├── domain/          # Entities, Value Objects, Port interfaces
├── application/     # Use cases, DTOs
├── infrastructure/  # Adapters (web, persistence, messaging, external)
└── config/          # Spring configuration only
```

## Team Conventions

### What We DO
- {Convention 1 — e.g., "Constructor injection only — zero @Autowired on fields"}
- {Convention 2 — e.g., "All REST responses wrapped in ApiResponse<T>"}
- {Convention 3 — e.g., "@Transactional(readOnly=true) at service class level, override for writes"}
- {Convention 4 — e.g., "All entities use UUID primary keys generated by Postgres"}
- {Convention 5 — e.g., "Flyway migrations follow V{n}__{verb}_{noun}.sql naming"}

### What We DON'T DO
- {Anti-pattern 1 — e.g., "No business logic in Controllers or Adapters"}
- {Anti-pattern 2 — e.g., "No JPA entities in API responses — always map to DTOs"}
- {Anti-pattern 3 — e.g., "No @Transactional on repositories or controllers"}
- {Anti-pattern 4 — e.g., "No Optional.get() without orElseThrow() or isPresent()"}

## Available Copilot CLI Agents
Run these in Copilot CLI for specialized tasks:

- `/new-feature` — plan and implement a new feature end-to-end
- `/fix` — diagnose and fix a bug systematically
- `/code-review` — Java-specific tiered review (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM)
- `/pr-review` — review an existing GitHub PR via GitHub MCP
- `/refactor` — restructure code while preserving behavior
- `/secure` — security audit and hardening
- `/doc-writer` — Javadoc, README, ADR, OpenAPI annotations
- `/write-a-commit` — generate conventional commit from staged changes
- `/explore` — understand unfamiliar code or trace a behavior
